explicit_statements: The mismatch is NOT a cohort-anchor mutation: the manifest file has a single git commit and has never been altered since it was frozen.
The mismatch is NOT a harmless content-preserving rewrite either, because no rewrite occurred at all -- the file is unchanged.

The mismatch is a STALE/INCORRECT DIGEST CLAIM: the value 82bbda32... asserted in the prior turn's prompt does not match the raw file bytes, does not match any reproducible canonical-digest convention, and -- critically -- was never the digest actually recorded by any of the three already-qualified downstream B2N artifacts.
All downstream B2N provenance/review artifacts (P2D resolution, human review packet, human review index) were built against and are bound to 54481980..., the correct and actual manifest digest.

Cohort content equivalence is fully proven: 20/20 members, ordinals 1-20, 20 unique mints, 20 unique census_event_ids, observation_required=true uniformly, zero field-level differences against downstream consumers.

erratum_p2f.supersedes_conclusion: The original 'reproducibility_attempts' section above concluded that 82bbda32...eedc did not correspond to any reproducible digest convention. That was incomplete, not wrong about the raw-file digest, but wrong about 82bbda32 being merely stale.
erratum_p2f.corrected_finding: During B2N-P3 executor inspection, src/acquisition/b2n_qualification.py's B2NManifest.digest() method was run directly against the real 20-member frozen manifest content. It deterministically produces 82bbda32d25a9951a8d8475528d7db3a92b675aae90ce2d55e13391a6b69eedc -- an EXACT match. This is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, compact separators, trailing newline) of the ordered [asdict(member) for member in members] list, which was not among the two reproduction methods originally tried.
erratum_p2f.corrected_conclusion: There are TWO distinct, both-correct digests for this manifest, each serving a different purpose: (1) 54481980...4d4c is the raw-file SHA-256, used by every P2D/P2E provenance/review artifact as the checkpoint/source-manifest identity; (2) 82bbda32...eedc is B2NManifest.digest() -- the executor's canonical member-list digest, which is what B2NQualificationRunAuthorization.manifest_digest and B2NManifest.validate() actually check at runtime. Neither digest is stale or incorrect; they are not interchangeable and must each be bound to their correct role in any B2N-P3 authorization artifact.
erratum_p2f.action: B2N-P3 authorization binds both digests explicitly under distinct field names (frozen_manifest_file_sha256 and b2n_manifest_digest_executor) rather than treating either as sole canonical value.
